## PCI PM callback reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

In `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/`, the PCI device PM table wires the system-suspend callback directly to `i915_pm_suspend`:

```c
static const struct dev_pm_ops i915_pm_ops = {
	.suspend		= i915_pm_suspend,
	.resume			= i915_pm_resume,
	.freeze			= i915_pm_freeze,
	.thaw			= i915_pm_thaw,
	.poweroff		= i915_pm_poweroff,
	.restore		= i915_pm_restore,
	.runtime_suspend	= i915_pm_runtime_suspend,
	.runtime_resume		= i915_pm_runtime_resume,
};
```

The call chain is therefore:

```text
PCI/system PM core
  └── dev_pm_ops.suspend
        └── i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
              └── i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
                    └── intel_display_suspend(struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv)
```

The other system-PM callbacks are separate entry points:

```text
.freeze   ──> i915_pm_freeze
.thaw     ──> i915_pm_thaw
.poweroff ──> i915_pm_poweroff
.restore  ──> i915_pm_restore
.resume   ──> i915_pm_resume
```

They do not call `i915_pm_suspend`; they have their own suspend/resume paths and, where appropriate, may share lower-level helpers.

## Callers that also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

None of the callers in the `i915_pm_suspend` chain also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`.

`i915_pm_runtime_suspend` is registered independently as the runtime-PM callback:

```text
PCI runtime-PM core
  └── dev_pm_ops.runtime_suspend
        └── i915_pm_runtime_suspend
```

Thus:

```text
i915_pm_suspend       → system suspend path
i915_pm_runtime_suspend → runtime suspend path
```

They are sibling callbacks, not nested calls. The system suspend path may manipulate runtime-PM state internally, but it does not invoke the runtime callback itself.

## `dev_priv` data flow

The pointer flow from `i915_pm_suspend` through `i915_drm_suspend` to `intel_display_suspend` is:

```text
struct device *kdev
  │
  ├── to_pci_dev(kdev)
  │      └── struct pci_dev *pdev
  │
  ├── pci_get_drvdata(pdev)
  │      └── struct drm_device *dev
  │
  └── to_i915(dev)
         └── struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv
```

In outline:

```c
static int i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct pci_dev *pdev = to_pci_dev(kdev);
	struct drm_device *dev = pci_get_drvdata(pdev);
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);

	return i915_drm_suspend(dev);
}
```

`i915_drm_suspend()` receives the `struct drm_device *`, derives the same private i915 object, and passes it to display suspend:

```c
static int i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);

	/* suspend preparation and device quiescing */

	intel_display_suspend(dev_priv);

	/* remaining suspend operations */
}
```

So the essential data flow is:

```text
kdev
 → pdev
 → dev
 → dev_priv
 → intel_display_suspend(dev_priv)
```

## PCI PM callback reaching `i915_pm_suspend`

In `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/`, the PCI device PM table wires the system-suspend callback directly to `i915_pm_suspend`:

```c
static const struct dev_pm_ops i915_pm_ops = {
	.suspend		= i915_pm_suspend,
	.resume			= i915_pm_resume,
	.freeze			= i915_pm_freeze,
	.thaw			= i915_pm_thaw,
	.poweroff		= i915_pm_poweroff,
	.restore		= i915_pm_restore,
	.runtime_suspend	= i915_pm_runtime_suspend,
	.runtime_resume		= i915_pm_runtime_resume,
};
```

The call chain is therefore:

```text
PCI/system PM core
  └── dev_pm_ops.suspend
        └── i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
              └── i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
                    └── intel_display_suspend(struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv)
```

The other system-PM callbacks are separate entry points:

```text
.freeze   ──> i915_pm_freeze
.thaw     ──> i915_pm_thaw
.poweroff ──> i915_pm_poweroff
.restore  ──> i915_pm_restore
.resume   ──> i915_pm_resume
```

They do not call `i915_pm_suspend`; they have their own suspend/resume paths and, where appropriate, may share lower-level helpers.

## Callers that also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

None of the callers in the `i915_pm_suspend` chain also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`.

`i915_pm_runtime_suspend` is registered independently as the runtime-PM callback:

```text
PCI runtime-PM core
  └── dev_pm_ops.runtime_suspend
        └── i915_pm_runtime_suspend
```

Thus:

```text
i915_pm_suspend       → system suspend path
i915_pm_runtime_suspend → runtime suspend path
```

They are sibling callbacks, not nested calls. The system suspend path may manipulate runtime-PM state internally, but it does not invoke the runtime callback itself.

## `dev_priv` data flow

The pointer flow from `i915_pm_suspend` through `i915_drm_suspend` to `intel_display_suspend` is:

```text
struct device *kdev
  │
  ├── to_pci_dev(kdev)
  │      └── struct pci_dev *pdev
  │
  ├── pci_get_drvdata(pdev)
  │      └── struct drm_device *dev
  │
  └── to_i915(dev)
         └── struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv
```

In outline:

```c
static int i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
{
	struct pci_dev *pdev = to_pci_dev(kdev);
	struct drm_device *dev = pci_get_drvdata(pdev);
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);

	return i915_drm_suspend(dev);
}
```

`i915_drm_suspend()` receives the `struct drm_device *`, derives the same private i915 object, and passes it to display suspend:

```c
static int i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);

	/* suspend preparation and device quiescing */

	intel_display_suspend(dev_priv);

	/* remaining suspend operations */
}
```

So the essential data flow is:

```text
kdev
 → pdev
 → dev
 → dev_priv
 → intel_display_suspend(dev_priv)
```
